name: zephyr-mqtt-mcu

adapter_config.broker_name: Mosquitto 2.x -> Zephyr EviCon firmware (Arm Cortex-M3, QEMU mps2-an385, cutoff mode)

system_version: Zephyr v4.2.0 EviCon firmware (firmware/zephyr-mcu: the sources of firmware/zephyr-cutoff, board mps2/an385, Cortex-M3 under qemu-system-arm, Zephyr's TCP/IP stack and LAN9118 driver, cutoff mode) + eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.20 (evicon_review.py records the image SHA-256, the Zephyr revision and the QEMU version)

testbed.owner: VM-E qemu-system-arm -machine mps2-an385 -kernel zephyr-mcu-qemu.elf (user-mode networking: the plant evicon-plant -tcp 127.0.0.1:18092 is 10.0.2.2:18092 for the guest; VM-B's broker through QEMU's NAT)

notes: Run with: python3 evicon_review.py measure zephyr-mcu (release 077), after 'bash deploy/setup/build_iot.sh start' reports MCU_BUILD_OK. The same probes, parameters and repetitions as zephyr-mqtt (the native_sim measurement of the same sources), on the firmware built for an Arm Cortex-M3 MCU and run by QEMU: Zephyr's own TCP/IP stack and Ethernet driver instead of the host's sockets, NVS on a simulated flash instead of a file. The MCU image has no command line: device zephyr-1, cutoff mode, VM-B's broker and the plant at 10.0.2.2 are Kconfig values of the build, which the driver checks against the testbed before it runs. Fault model as zephyr-mqtt: network loss/delay, client abandon; owner up.
fault_model: network loss/delay, client abandon; owner up (no owner crash or reboot)
